rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 9 (base_speed 1.1, kp 2.6, kd 0.9, ki 0.05, x ±0.03 m, last_direction) scored 704.85, the best raced design so far. Oval finished 20/20 (mean 1.87 s) and s-bend 20/20 (mean 2.25 s), so the speed margin to the 3 s limit holds. The slalom still ended 0/20 off track, and its max_error rose to 0.0661 from 0.0618 at base_speed 1.2. Line-loss events rose to 1.35. Lower speed therefore did not clear the slalom limit. Its score gain came from the oval and s-bend, not from the slalom. Across iterations 3 to 9 the slalom max_error has stayed between 0.0618 and 0.0661 under every kp, kd, ki, x-coverage and speed setting tried. The Evaluator's decision rule for this case says the controller levers are largely exhausted and the next structural test is line_loss 'search_right'. Slalom line-loss events have stayed near 1.0 to 1.35 throughout, so the way the robot re-acquires the line after a loss is the untested lever.

Change. line_loss changes from 'last_direction' to 'search_right', and nothing else changes. Geometry stays at iteration 9 (x ±0.03 m at y 0.06, 16 mm footprint, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03). Controller stays at base_speed 1.1, kp 2.6, ki 0.05, kd 0.9, sensor_weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]. This is a single-variable test against iteration 9. 'search_right' fixes the loss signal at +1, which steers the robot to its LEFT. The hypothesis is that a fixed sweep direction may recover the line on the slalom better than repeating the last signal, which may be the wrong side after an alternating bend.

Expected result. Oval and s-bend stay near 20/20 because line losses there are rare (0.5 and 0.15 per run). The slalom line-loss count may fall or change pattern. A slalom finish is possible but not expected. Risk: the fixed left sweep could worsen s-bend or oval recovery, in which case the next step is to return to 'last_direction' at base_speed 1.1.

Decision rules for the next iteration. If oval or s-bend finish rate falls below 0.95, or s-bend completion_time exceeds about 2.8 s, return line_loss to 'last_direction'. If the slalom still ends off track with max_error at or above 0.06, test 'search_left' with everything else unchanged, which is the other fixed-direction option. If any slalom run finishes, hold all values and confirm the score.

Hypotheses. (a) The line-loss response, not the gains, sets slalom max_error. (b) 'search_right' changes the slalom line-loss count compared with the 1.35 seen in iteration 9. Measurements requested: full set, read per track, with emphasis on slalom line_loss_events, max_error, progress and completion, and on oval and s-bend completion_time.
